title: vps-server
login_locked: Too many attempts. Try again in {seconds}s.
server_label_invalid: Use up to 40 letters, numbers, spaces, hyphens, underscores, or periods.
server_label_error: Could not save the server label.
password_changed: Password changed. Sign in with the new password.
access_load_error: The saved IP list could not be read. Password sign-in still works; adding a valid IP replaces the damaged list.
access_ip_invalid: Enter one private IPv4 or unique-local IPv6 address.
access_ip_error: Could not save the IP list.
access_password_invalid: Passwords must match and the new password must be 12–128 characters.
your_ip: Your IP as seen by this server
test_info: Latency is measured first over {pings} round trips, then each direction runs for about {sec}s over several parallel connections; the first {warm}s of each are a warmup and not counted.
visitors_clear_confirm: Clear all recent visitor history? This cannot be undone. New visits and active connections will be recorded again.
visitors_clear_done: History cleared. New visits and active connections will be recorded again.
visitors_clear_failed: Could not clear history. Try again.
changelog_missing: doc/LOG.md or its Changelog section was not found next to the app, so there is nothing to show here.
changelog_fallback: The Chinese changelog is not available in this install; showing the English one.
development_fallback: Current test-build notes are available in English only.
visitors_info: Covers every device with a TCP connection to this host on any port — established, half-open or closing — sampled from the kernel every {sec}s, plus HTTP requests to this page. "out" marks connections this machine opened itself. TCP only: UDP (DNS, VPN, QUIC) and ICMP are not visible to this method, and connections that come and go between two samples can still be missed.
visitors_info_http_only: Connection tracking is off, so this only covers HTTP requests to this page.
iperf_port_invalid: Port unavailable or the window is running.
iperf_disabled: The iperf3 window is switched off in this install (VPSSRV_IPERF_ENABLE=0).
iperf_missing: iperf3 is not installed on this host. Install it with: apt install iperf3
iperf_port_busy: Port {port} is already in use, so iperf3 could not start.
iperf_info: The window always closes itself — there is no "leave it running" option, because an open iperf3 server lets anyone saturate this host's uplink. Latency is the mean_rtt field of the JSON output.
iperf_client_invalid: Check the server IP, port, duration, rate, protocol, and direction.
iperf_client_missing: iperf3 is not installed on this host.
iperf_client_busy: Another outbound test is already running.
iperf_client_timeout: The target did not finish the test in time.
iperf_client_failed: The test failed. Check the target server and its firewall.
anytls_not_installed: The anytls module is not installed on this host. To add it: sudo VPSSRV_MODULES=anytls bash deploy/install.sh
anytls_state_stopped: Installed on port {port}, but the service is not running. Check: systemctl status {service}
anytls_sni: SNI (read back from the certificate CN)
anytls_host_note: Addresses come from host interfaces and optional Tailscale. If needed, edit the server address after copying the link.
anytls_warning: This page shows the node password in clear. It is behind the console login and never appears on the public page, but do not paste a screenshot of it anywhere.
anytls_reset_confirm: I understand that every existing client stops working
node_overview_intro: Manage connection details and node settings in one place.
total_over: The total traffic limit is reached. This only warns for now; nothing is throttled or cut off.
total_warn: More than 80% of the total traffic limit is used.
total_hint: Adds up nodes, FRPS, domain forwarding, port forwarding, FRPC, Tailscale, iperf3, Mini Drive and speed test, counted as on their own pages (forwarded traffic ×2). Reset times are the server's local time; console pages, the terminal and SSH are not counted.
traffic_help_once: Upload is traffic coming into this host, download is traffic leaving it; each byte counts once. At the traffic cap it is slowed to 1 Mbps or cut off, as set.
traffic_help_twice: Forwarded traffic enters and leaves this host, so it counts twice, like a Singbox node. At the traffic cap it is slowed to 1 Mbps or cut off, as set.
traffic_help_tailscale: Counts traffic on the tailscale0 interface; traffic this host forwards (exit node, subnet routes) enters and leaves it, so it counts twice. At the traffic cap it is slowed to 1 Mbps or cut off, as set.
traffic_frpc_shared: These instances connect to the same server, so their traffic is counted and limited together: {names}
files_error_traffic_blocked: Mini Drive reached its traffic cap or validity period; uploads and downloads are paused.
node_meter_suspect: Incomplete metering; usage may be undercounted
node_random_confirm: Confirm random port and credential reset; SNI stays unchanged.
node_settings_failed: Node settings could not be applied.
node_state_unavailable: Node state is unavailable. Run the installer again to migrate or repair this installation, then reload this page.
proxy_not_installed: Singbox is not installed on this server. Install it from Settings → Modules.
proxy_state_stopped: Installed, but the service is not running. Check: systemctl status {service}
proxy_host_note: Addresses come from host interfaces and optional Tailscale. If needed, edit the server address after copying the link.
portfwd_module_disabled: Port forwarding is switched off in this install (VPSSRV_PORTFWD_ENABLE=0).
portfwd_apply_failed: Forward could not be applied. Check the host firewall.
portfwd_invalid: Check the port numbers (1–65535) and the target IP — one of them was not valid.
portfwd_port_taken: That public port is already used by this host or by another forward.
portfwd_howto: Uses this host's own iptables (DNAT + MASQUERADE); traffic passes through here on the way to the target, so the target sees this host as the client, not the original visitor. net.ipv4.ip_forward is turned on automatically the first time a forward is enabled, and is left on afterwards even if every forward is later removed — turning it back off is not automatic, since other software on this host may depend on it too.
probe_your_ip: The server sees your IP address
log_firewall_open: Could not open port {port} via {backend}; adjust the firewall by hand if the test cannot connect.
log_firewall_close: Could not close port {port} via {backend}; adjust the firewall by hand if the test cannot connect.
log_iperf_stuck: iperf3 (pid {pid}) did not exit after SIGKILL; closing the window anyway
log_iperf_release_failed: Could not release the iperf3 port registration ({error}); continuing
log_portfwd_release_failed: Could not release a port forwarding registration ({error}); continuing
log_iptables_missing: iptables not found; the port-forward rule was not applied.
log_portfwd_apply: Could not fully apply port forward {rule_id}; check iptables by hand.
log_public_conflict: Public port {port} is also the console port; skipping that public listener.
log_public_bind: Could not bind public port {port} ({error}); continuing without it. Something else may already hold it — check `ss -lntp`.
log_tracking: Tracking inbound connections from the kernel TCP table every {seconds:g}s
log_tracking_unavailable: VPSSRV_TRACK_CONNECTIONS=1 but /proc/net/tcp is unavailable; the visitor log will only cover requests to this web app.
log_iperf_missing: VPSSRV_IPERF_ENABLE=1 but iperf3 is not installed; the console will say so when a window is requested (apt install iperf3).
node_route_hint: Format: IP, IP:port, network (10.0.0.0/24), domain, *.domain; a port is 443 or 8000-8100; IPv6 with a port is [fd00::1]:443. “Public Internet only” refuses private, loopback, link-local and 100.64.0.0/10 addresses; “Only the destinations below” refuses everything else. Domains are judged by the addresses they resolve to.
node_delete_confirm: Delete this node and revoke its share link?
login_ip_unavailable: This IP cannot use password-free access. Sign in with the password and add a private LAN IP in Settings.
node_keep_port: Leave blank to keep current port
frp_client_note: FRPC instances on this host can be configured below. Existing connections stay active until you edit them.
frp_address_note: Use an address reachable from each FRPC instance. Add proxy entries in that instance’s configuration.
frp_client_unavailable: Install FRPS to see a client configuration.
login_ban_switch: Ban IPs with too many failures
login_ban_rule: After {count} wrong passwords from one IP (IPv6 grouped by /64) within {window}s, it is banned: {first} the first time, ten times longer for each repeat within a day, at most {max}. A successful login clears its count.
login_ban_observe_hint: When off, failures are still counted and a threshold hit is flagged instead of banned, so you can test detection. Switching clears current bans and flags.
login_ban_empty: No failed logins since the web console started.
login_ban_disabled: Failed login ban turned off. Failures are still recorded.
login_ban_cleared: Failed login records and bans cleared.
login_ban_error: Could not save the failed login ban setting.
login_ban_load_error: The failed login ban settings file is invalid; the ban is treated as on.
login_global_rule: When all sources together get {count} wrong passwords within {window}s, password login pauses for {duration} for addresses that never logged in successfully.
login_global_flagged: Global threshold reached, not paused ({seconds}s left).
log_login_global: Too many failed logins overall: password login paused for unknown addresses for {seconds}s (last from {ip})
log_login_global_observed: Too many failed logins overall; ban is off, recorded only (last from {ip})
alert_ban_body: {ip} entered wrong passwords repeatedly and is banned for {seconds}s.
alert_global_body: Many addresses are entering wrong passwords; password login is paused for unknown addresses for {seconds}s.
alert_test_body: If you see this, login alerts can reach you.
console_access_intro: When on, only listed addresses can connect to the console; others are dropped before the TLS handshake and never see the login page. Loopback is always allowed. LAN devices, Clash subscriptions included, must be listed too.
console_access_recovery: If you are locked out, run this as root on the server to turn the limit off; no restart needed:
console_access_invalid: Enter a single IP address or a CIDR network.
console_access_too_wide: A network covering every address cannot be added.
console_access_need_current: Add the current address first, or turning this on would lock you out.
console_access_keep_current: Removing this would lock out the current connection. Turn the limit off or add another entry that covers it first.
console_access_error: Could not save the console access list.
console_access_load_error: The console access list file is invalid; the limit is treated as off.
sessions_intro: A login lasts at most {ttl} and ends after {idle} without activity.
sessions_revoked: The selected devices were signed out.
sessions_use_logout: Use Log out for this device.
alerts_intro: Push logins from new addresses and failed-login bans to your phone through Bark. The key is the last part of the push URL in the Bark app.
alerts_status_off: No push key; no alerts are sent.
alerts_on_new_ip: Alert on login from a new address
alerts_on_ban: Alert when a ban is triggered
alerts_test_sent: Test alert sent; check your phone.
alerts_test_failed: The test alert failed. Check the server address, the key and the host's network.
alerts_invalid: The server must start with https:// or http://; the key may contain only letters, digits, - and _.
alerts_error: Could not save the login alert settings.
alerts_load_error: The login alert settings file is invalid; alerts are treated as not set up.
audit_intro: The latest 50 logins and security setting changes, kept on the server (up to 500).
log_login_ban: Too many failed logins: {ip} failed {count} times, banned for {seconds}s
log_login_ban_observed: Too many failed logins: {ip} failed {count} times; ban is off, recorded only
modules_note: Install or uninstall optional modules here. Short-lived progress appears below; detailed logs have a separate page. Use the switches on Home to enable or disable features.
logs_clear_confirm: Clear the currently displayed history? System logs will be retained.
logs_clear_done: Historical logs shown here have been cleared.
module_source_missing: Installer files are unavailable. Upgrade from a complete checkout first.
module_tailscale_asset_missing: The bundled Tailscale archive is missing. Rerun deploy/install.sh from complete source or an offline Release bundle containing the third_party/tailscale archive, extracted into a separate directory, while preserving the existing installation and state directories, then retry.
host_check_nft_missing: This host has no usable nftables. Run apt install nftables first.
host_check_nft_unusable: nftables on this host cannot read the firewall rules. Run apt install nftables first.
host_check_nft_auto: This host has no usable nftables. Installing the module installs it with apt automatically.
login_cert_missing: This browser did not present a valid client certificate.
login_password_disabled: Certificate login is on. The password cannot sign in; it only confirms sensitive actions.
client_cert_required_text: This console only accepts devices with an imported client certificate. Import one, then fully quit and reopen the browser. If the certificate is lost, follow the README to restore password login as root on the server.
client_cert_intro: Log in with a certificate instead of, or together with, the password: generate a certificate for each device, import it into the system or browser, and the browser presents it when the console opens. Choose the login method below; with "Certificate only" or "Password + certificate", a device without a certificate cannot even open the login page.
client_cert_current_none: This connection did not present a certificate.
client_cert_need_current: Import a certificate and reopen the console with it (this page then shows the certificate in use) before turning this on, so you cannot lock yourself out.
client_cert_keep_current: While certificates are required, the certificate this connection uses cannot be revoked.
client_cert_error: The certificate operation failed; the certificate files may not be writable.
client_cert_openssl_missing: The bundled openssl is missing, so certificates cannot be generated. Running the installer again restores it.
client_cert_tls_unsupported: This host's TLS library cannot verify client certificates (self test failed), so certificates are disabled. Update the system openssl/libssl packages, then generate a certificate again.
client_cert_name_invalid: The device name must be 1 to 40 characters.
client_cert_issued_text: Note the import password. It is shown only once and the server keeps no private key; after leaving this page you can only generate a new one.
client_cert_steps_title: Next, complete these three steps in order
client_cert_step_download: Download the certificate file. Downloading alone is not enough: browsers do not read certificates from the Downloads folder.
client_cert_step_import: Import it into the system certificate store, entering the import password above:
client_cert_os_windows: Windows: double-click the file, choose Current User as the store location and Personal as the store (or let the wizard choose).
client_cert_os_macos: macOS: double-click the file and add it to the login keychain.
client_cert_os_android: Android: Settings > Security > Encryption & credentials > Install a certificate > VPN & app user certificate, then pick the file.
client_cert_os_ios: iOS / iPadOS: open it in Files, then install it under Settings > Profile Downloaded.
client_cert_os_firefox: Firefox does not use the system store by default: import it separately under Settings > Privacy & Security > Certificates > View Certificates > Your Certificates.
client_cert_step_setup: Download the one-click setup file for this device's system and run it, entering the import password above when asked. It imports the certificate and makes Chrome and Edge pick it on their own from now on.
client_cert_manual: Manual import (Android, iOS, Firefox, or if the one-click setup fails)
client_cert_step_restart: Fully quit and reopen the browser. Closing the window is not enough: Chrome and Edge may keep running in the background. Open chrome://restart or edge://restart, or quit from the system tray.
client_cert_step_verify: Reopen the console's security settings. Once the certificate in use is shown, turn on Require client certificate. If the browser asks for a certificate, pick this one.
client_cert_autoselect: Stop picking the certificate every time
client_cert_setup_macos: Double-click, then install it in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Profiles
client_cert_setup_linux: Run it in a terminal with bash
cert_setup_nss_missing: certutil and pk12util are missing; install libnss3-tools (Debian/Ubuntu) or nss-tools (Fedora) first.
cert_setup_done_linux: Done. Fully quit the browser and open it again.
cert_setup_found: The certificate is already in the current user's store.
cert_setup_unc: Running from a network location: the “UNC paths are not supported” note from CMD above can be ignored; setup goes on as usual.
cert_setup_imported_linux: Certificate imported into the browser's certificate store.
cert_setup_missing: This computer does not have the certificate. Import it first, or download the script that includes it from the page shown after issuing.
cert_setup_machine: Note: an administrator policy of the same name exists on this computer and overrides this setting:
cert_setup_no_browser: Neither Chrome nor Edge was found.
cert_setup_done: Done. Fully quit the browser and open it again (chrome://restart or edge://restart).
client_cert_current_none_hint: No certificate on this device yet? Each device uses its own: enter a device name below to generate one; the page that follows has one-click setup files. If you already imported one and still see this, the browser was most likely not fully restarted.
host_check_tun_missing: This host has no /dev/net/tun. Enable TUN/TAP in the VPS control panel.
host_check_tailscale_conflict: A system tailscaled.service is already running. Stop it first.
frp_server_edit_note: The port or token change restarts FRPS. Update clients that use the old values.
frp_token_keep: Leave the token blank to keep the current value.
frp_client_binary_missing: FRPC is not installed on this host.
frp_client_edit_note: Edit the TOML configuration. Saving verifies it and restarts an active instance.
frp_save_failed: FRP update failed. Existing settings were restored when possible.
frp_port_keep: Leave blank to keep the current port
frp_unsupported_config: This FRPC configuration has settings the field editor cannot represent.
frp_delete_client_confirm: Delete FRPC instance {name}? Its configuration will be saved for recovery.
module_uninstall_confirm: Uninstall {name}? Its configuration and nodes are kept and backed up on the server, and restored when you install it again.
console_port_started: The port change has started. Wait a few seconds, then open the new address.
console_port_invalid: Enter an unused port from 1024 to 65535.
console_port_error: Could not change the port. The original address is still available.
tailscale_action_failed: Action failed; check the service logs
tailscale_exit_lan: Allow local LAN with exit node
tailscale_web_open_failed: Could not open the Tailscale web interface
tailscale_logout_confirm: Confirm logout; the current Tailscale connection may drop and reauthentication will be required.
frp_saving: Saving settings. If the connection drops, the result will appear when it reconnects.
frp_forwarding_stcp: STCP visitors only: forwards to {local}:{port} (no public port)
frp_secret_keep: Blank: generated for a new proxy, current key kept when editing
frp_visitor_note: A visitor listens on 127.0.0.1 on this host and reaches an STCP proxy on another FRPC using the same FRPS token and STCP secret key. The port is never exposed externally.
nav.label: Navigation
module_held_by_domains: Ports 80 and 443 are used by domain forwarding or the IP certificate
domains_added: Added. The certificate is requested automatically once the name points here, usually within a minute or two.
domains_token_saved: Cloudflare token added and DNS records synced.
domains_token_cleared: Cloudflare token removed. Existing DNS records are left as they are.
domains_error_host_invalid: Invalid domain name. Enter a full name such as nas.example.com.
domains_error_port_invalid: The port must be 1 to 65535 and not 80 or 443.
domains_error_caddy_rejected: Caddy rejected the new configuration; the previous one was restored. See the detailed logs.
domains_error_failed: The change failed. See the detailed logs.
domains_dns_auth: Cloudflare rejected the token. Check that it is valid and can edit DNS for this domain.
domains_dns_zone: The token cannot see a Cloudflare zone for this domain.
domains_dns_unreachable: Cloudflare could not be reached; it will be retried.
domains_dns_api: Cloudflare returned an error; it will be retried.
domains_dns_no_token: No Cloudflare token yet; add the DNS records by hand.
domains_dns_no_address: This host has no public IP address to publish.
domains_token_help: Create an API token in Cloudflare with Zone > DNS > Edit for your domains. You can add several tokens (for example, domains in different Cloudflare accounts); each site uses the token that manages its main domain. Records are DNS only, and this host's IP is checked every 5 minutes.
domains_token_clear_confirm: Remove the token “{name}”? DNS records of its domains stop updating automatically; existing records stay as they are.
domains_token_name_placeholder: Optional, such as the account name
domains_error_token_rejected: Cloudflare rejected this token. Check that it is correct and has Zone > DNS > Edit.
domains_error_token_exists: This token has already been added.
domains_error_token_missing: That token no longer exists; it may have been removed.
domains_target_console: This console (Caddy checks the client certificate)
domains_add_help_zones: Add a subdomain under a main domain the Cloudflare token manages: nas becomes nas.<main domain>; @ means the main domain itself. DNS records and certificates are handled automatically.
domains_add_help_manual: No Cloudflare token yet: enter the full name and point it at this host yourself. With a token you can pick the main domain.
domains_cert_detail: {issuer}, valid until {date} ({days} days left), renewed automatically
domains_cert_pending_detail: Waiting: Caddy requests it once the name points here
domains_dns_detail: {kinds} record points here, DNS only; last synced {time}
domains_dns_manual: No token; point it here by hand
domains_error_zone_unknown: The token cannot see this main domain; reload the page and try again.
domains_zones_none: This token sees no main domains. Check its zone resources in Cloudflare.
domains_ip_help: The console's existing https://<this host's IP>:<port> switches to a Let's Encrypt certificate, so browsers stop warning. The certificate lasts about 6 days and Caddy renews it; the port and the client-certificate requirement stay the same, and 80/443 do not serve the console.
domains_ip_off_confirm: Stop using the IP certificate? The console goes back to its self-signed certificate and browsers will warn again.
domains_ip_enabled: Enabled. The certificate usually arrives within a minute; the console picks it up on its own.
domains_ip_disabled: IP certificate turned off; the console is back on its self-signed certificate.
domains_error_no_public_ip: This host has no public IPv4 address to certify.
domains_backend_tls: The backend speaks HTTPS (its certificate is not checked; fits self-signed NAS or router pages)
domains_upstream_host: Send the backend its own address as Host (for backends that only accept IP:port)
domains_site_disabled: Disabled. Requests to the name are dropped; DNS records and the certificate are kept.
domains_alert_ip_body: {old} → {new}; DNS records follow the new address.
domains_alert_dns_body: Cloudflare records for {host} could not be updated; see the domain forwarding page.
domains_alert_cert_body: The certificate for {host} expires {date} and has not been renewed; check ports 80/443 and DNS.
domains_aliases: Other names (optional, one per line, same target)
domains_allow_ips: Only these addresses or networks may connect (optional, one per line; empty means anyone)
domains_more_options: More options: other names, allowed addresses, password
domains_auth_help: Browsers ask for this user name and password first. Leave the user name empty for none.
domains_auth_keep: Leave empty to keep the current one
domains_error_allow_invalid: Invalid address or network (at most 32), e.g. 203.0.113.7 or 198.51.100.0/24.
domains_error_auth_invalid: The user name may use letters, digits and . _ -; a new password needs 8 to 128 characters.
files_quota_help: Whatever the limit, at least 500 MiB stays free on disk. Lowering it deletes nothing; new files just wait until there is room.
files_rate_help: All download links together stay under this speed; downloads running at the same time share it. Leave empty for no limit.
files_error_rate_invalid: Enter a limit from 0.1 to 10240, or leave it empty for no limit.
files_fetch_help: This server downloads it directly, for sources other hosts cannot reach (GitHub Releases, for example). You can close the browser; the download continues in the background.
files_link_help: Anyone with a download link can download without a password or certificate; share it only with those who need it.
files_delete_confirm: Delete "{name}" and all its download links?
files_error_no_room: Not enough room: over the limit, or less than 500 MiB would stay free on disk.
files_error_too_many: Too many files. Delete some first.
files_error_incomplete: The transfer stopped early; the partial file was discarded.
files_error_url_invalid: Enter an http or https URL.
files_error_url_blocked: This address points at this machine or a link-local address and is not allowed.
files_error_busy: Three downloads are already running. Wait for them to finish.
files_error_not_found: Not found; it may have been deleted.
files_error_too_many_links: This file has too many links. Revoke some first.
files_error_quota_invalid: The limit must be between 0.1 and 10240 GiB.
ipcert_pending: Being issued: usually within a minute, then the console switches to it
ipcert_ports: Port 80 must be reachable from the internet (Let's Encrypt validates through it). While on, Caddy holds 80/443 and serves the public reachability page, using this certificate for https://<this IP>/ too. No domain or Cloudflare token is needed.
ipcert_failed: The change failed: there may be no public IPv4. See Settings > Detailed logs.
files_upload_help: Choose a file and upload it; up to {room}.
client_cert_autoselect_help: Download the file for this device's system and run it; from then on the browser picks this certificate for the console without asking.
module_public_needs_ipcert: HTTPS needs the IP certificate on
backup_contents: A backup holds all configuration and state: console settings, certificates and keys, nodes, FRP, domain forwarding, the Tailscale login and the service unit files. It does not include program code or the files in Mini Drive. Backups contain keys, so keep downloaded files safe.
backup_schedule_help: Backs up on the schedule you choose (repeating, or only once) and, for repeating ones, keeps only the latest few scheduled backups; manual and pre-upgrade backups are not affected.
backup_delete_confirm: Delete this backup? This cannot be undone.
backup_upload_help: Upload a backup file you downloaded earlier. After it is checked it appears in the list, where you can restore it.
backup_msg_restore_started: Restoring and restarting services; reload the page in a moment.
backup_error_invalid: The input or file is not valid.
task_delete_confirm: Delete the task {name} and its run history? This cannot be undone.
task_run_as_root: The command runs as root on the server and is stopped after the timeout; a task is not started again while its previous run is still going. The latest 20 runs are kept for each task.
task_msg_started: Started; reload in a moment to see the result.
task_error_invalid: The task settings are not valid.
task_error_limit: The task limit has been reached.
task_month_day_help: 1 to 31; in a month without that day, its last day.
task_schedule_help: Five fields: minute hour day month weekday, for example */15 * * * * is every 15 minutes; @daily and @hourly also work.
login_mode_hint: Before switching to "Certificate only" or "Password + certificate", open this page with an active certificate (the one in use is shown above), or you lock yourself out. If you lose the certificate, run `python3 /root/apps/vps-server/src/web/client_cert.py disable` on the server to go back to password only.
login_mode_password_help: Only the password logs in; a certificate the browser sends is ignored.
login_mode_cert_help: Only a client certificate logs in; a device without one reaches nothing. The terminal and security settings still ask for the password.
login_mode_either_help: Either the password or a certificate logs in.
login_mode_both_help: The device must present a valid certificate and the password must be entered; one alone is not enough.
login_cert_disabled: The current login method does not allow certificate login.
backup_enc_on_text: New backups are encrypted to your public key. This server holds only the public key and cannot open them itself; restoring asks for the private key you saved. Public key fingerprint {fp}.
backup_enc_off_text: Backups are not encrypted right now, and they leave out the data key (so they restore only on this host). After you generate a key pair, backups are encrypted and carry the data key, so they restore on any host.
backup_enc_regenerate_confirm: A key is already set. After regenerating, new backups open only with the new private key; existing encrypted backups still need the old one. Continue?
backup_enc_own: Or use a public key you already have (Base64)
backup_key_page_text: The private key is shown only here, once, and the server does not keep it. Copy it now and store it safely; without it the encrypted backups cannot be opened.
backup_key_done: I have saved it, go back
backup_error_key_wrong: The private key is wrong, or the backup is damaged.
backup_error_key_needed: This backup is encrypted; enter its private key.
data_enc_on_text: The console's password, sessions, alert key, audit records, access lists, Mini Drive index and scheduled tasks are stored encrypted ({encrypted}/{total} files). The data key is /etc/vps-server/data.key; do not back it up beside the data. Node, FRP, domain forwarding and Tailscale configuration must be read by those programs as they are, so it is not covered here but by the encrypted backups.
data_enc_off_text: This host has no data key yet, so data is stored in plain text. Running the installer again (an upgrade) creates /etc/vps-server/data.key and turns encryption on.
data_enc_error_text: The encryption status cannot be read; check /etc/vps-server/data.key.
log_encryption_off: No data key; state files are stored in plain text (running the installer again creates one)
total_multiplier_note: Each figure is billed usage: nodes, FRPS and forwarding count every byte twice (in and out), so it is double what that feature's own page shows. The period runs from the reset day and includes what each source has already used in its current cycle.
total_actual_gib: Usage the provider shows for this period (GiB)
total_calibrate_hint: The count can differ from what the provider bills. Enter the usage shown in the provider's panel for this period; the console stores the difference as a "calibration", shows it as its own bar above and includes it in the total; it clears itself when the next period begins. Leave it empty and save to clear the calibration.
backup_result_ok: Restored {files} files from {name}. The state before is saved as a "Before restore" backup.
backup_result_failed: Not completed: {name} — {error}. The current configuration was not changed.
backup_error_ack_needed: This backup has risks; tick the confirmation before restoring.
backup_restore_needs_key: This backup is encrypted. Enter its private key to see what is inside. The key is used for this one step and is not stored.
backup_restore_other_key: This backup is sealed to a different backup key than the one set now, so the current private key may not open it; you need the private key that matches it.
backup_restore_this_key: This backup is sealed to the current backup key.
backup_restore_warn_host: This backup comes from another host ({host}). Restoring it overwrites this host with its configuration, including the data key, login method and certificates.
backup_restore_warn_newer: This backup comes from a newer version ({version}) than the one running; restoring it may be incompatible.
backup_restore_ack: I understand the risks above and still want to restore
backup_restore_effect: Restoring overwrites the current configuration with the backup's and restarts the related services; the console disconnects briefly. The current state is backed up first, and the result is shown at the top of the Backup page.
task_error_past: That time has already passed; choose a time in the future.
backup_error_past: That time has already passed; choose a time in the future.
monitor_alert_cpu_body: CPU at {percent}% for more than {minutes} minutes
